messages:
Anna: Heads-up — ran into confusing error shapes in the Python sample app during onboarding. 401 surfaces as a generic ApiError with no typed info, 429 has no retry hint/header parsed, and the message text is pretty vague. Any plan for SDK ergonomics (typed exceptions, retry metadata) so apps can give better UX?
Mike: +1 saw this in Node sample too. The exception hierarchy is inconsistent across languages.
Jessica: Can you paste the raw error?
Anna: Sure — from quick repro: `ApiError: request failed (status=401)` and stack. No error.code or typed class. 429 shows `RateLimited` string in body but SDK throws same ApiError.
Oleg: This is painful for customers. We should map HTTP codes to typed exceptions like `AuthError`, `RateLimitError(retry_after)`, `ServerError`.
Sara: Agree. Also include retry metadata on the exception object: `retry_after`, `retryable: true`, and ideally `retry_strategy` if we parsed `Retry-After` or `RateLimit-Reset`.
Mike: For parity we need canonical names across SDKs. Proposal: AuthError (401/403), RateLimitError (429) with numeric `retry_after_ms`, ClientError (4xx else), ServerError (5xx). Add a base `RedwoodError` with `httpStatus` and `raw` payload.
Jessica: Example JS shape suggestion: ```class RateLimitError extends RedwoodError { constructor(msg, retryAfterMs){ super(msg); this.retryAfterMs = retryAfterMs; this.retryable = true; } }```
Anna: And Python: ```class RateLimitError(RedwoodError):
    def __init__(self, msg, retry_after_ms: Optional[int]=None):
        super().__init__(msg)
        self.retry_after_ms = retry_after_ms
        self.retryable = True
```
Oleg: Also important: surface whether error is idempotent-safe to retry automatically. Maybe `retry_idempotent_ok` boolean. For non-idempotent routes, SDK should not auto-retry unless explicit.
Mike: There are auth flows where 401 means token expired and we can refresh automatically. We should expose an interface for automatic token refresh hooks in SDKs.
Jessica: UX note — error messages shown in sample apps should be user-friendly: avoid raw HTTP messages. Provide `user_message` on error or a mapping helper `formatErrorForUser(err)` in devex samples.
Anna: For onboarding friction: sample app readme currently suggests catching `ApiError` only. We should update to catch specific types with fallback. Quick patch idea in sample: ```try { ... } catch (err) { if (err instanceof RateLimitError) { showToast('Rate limit, retrying...'); } else if (err instanceof AuthError) { redirectToLogin(); } else { showToast('Something went wrong'); } }```
Sara: How about backward compatibility? Many customers already catching `ApiError`. We must keep `ApiError` as base but encourage migration. Deprecation warning could be logged when only generic shape is used.
Oleg: Also ensure errors include stable `code` strings (e.g., `auth_invalid_token`, `rate_limit_exceeded`) in the JSON body — useful for clients that pattern-match instead of instanceof.
Mike: Implementation owner? I can take Node + sample app. Jessica can do Python. Oleg can spec the canonical mapping and JSON schema.
Jessica: I'll open a PR with Python exception classes and tests for parsing `Retry-After` and `RateLimit-Reset` headers.
Anna: Thanks — I can update the sample app to demonstrate `formatErrorForUser` and catch blocks.
Sara: Devex docs: add a short migration guide: "Handling SDK errors: typed exceptions & retry metadata" and a snippet for each SDK.
ci-bot: Reminder: link to the design RFC template when creating the mapping PR — https://redwood.internal/rfcs  :robot_face:
Oleg: One more detail — add structured `hint` field for machine-readable remediation suggestions (e.g., `remediation: refresh_token|backoff|contact_support`). That helps product UIs show next steps.
Mike: Sounds good. Proposed next steps: 1) Oleg drafts canonical mapping + codes, 2) SDK owners implement typed classes + payload parsing, 3) sample apps + docs updated, 4) tests + migration notes. I'll file an umbrella issue.
Anna: ETA?
Jessica: I can get a first pass in 48h for Python tests.
Mike: Node PR in 72h.
Oleg: I'll aim for a spec doc by EOD.
Anna: Great — thanks all. :thumbsup:
